statement: Improve DFM-Mamba (discrete flow matching on Mamba) so that after training, wikitext word perplexity measured by lm-eval decreases, without changing the evaluation protocol or using extra evaluation data.
domain: discrete flow matching / state space models
subfield: DFM-Mamba training and wikitext language modeling
source_paper: Mamba-3: Improved Sequence Modeling using State Space Principles (arXiv:2603.15569) with the DFM-Mamba path
constraints: Evaluate with lm-eval task wikitext and report word_perplexity (lower is better)
Use the same tokenizer, context length, and evaluation split for every candidate
Match the training budget across candidates unless the idea explicitly changes it
The GPU server is offline: use preinstalled packages and local data/model caches
Do not train on wikitext test data
Do not modify bench/rsi_dfm_train_eval.py or bench/dfm_lm_eval.py

directions.title: DFM training objective
directions.description: Change the discrete flow-matching objective or time/noise schedule while keeping the Mamba backbone and tokenizer fixed.

directions.title: block and context schedule
directions.description: Improve block length, context handling, or training sequence composition for language modeling.

directions.title: optimization recipe
directions.description: Improve optimization, data ordering, or precision handling without changing the evaluation protocol.

forbidden: changing the lm-eval task or word_ppl metric
changing the tokenizer or evaluation split
audience_note: Real repository benchmark: the target project trains a DFM-Mamba checkpoint and evaluates wikitext word perplexity with lm-eval on a GPU server. The remote runner rsyncs the local git worktree, sets CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, and executes over SSH; the server does not need network access.
